Defined by immunodeficiency and ectodermal defects; sweat, hair and dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Recurrent infections do not establish additional organ damage.
Myeloid blood and marrow malignancy; possible disseminated intravascular coagulation remains within the haematologic axis.
Down syndrome causes neurodevelopmental impairment; congenital heart defects affect ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, and functional ocular abnormalities over 50%.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the renal pelvis.
Corneal hydrops complicating keratoconus, with corneal edema and potential scarring.
Hepatic lipid storage/fibrosis defines disease; intestinal storage with steatorrhea is reported in 80-99%. Cognitive injury is not typical across subtypes.
Subchondral bone necrosis and osteochondral fragmentation directly damage joints.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy with bilateral epithelial microcysts and opacities.
Degeneration confined to the peripheral cornea.
Deafness, vitiligo and achalasia define the syndrome; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%. EEG abnormalities alone do not establish neurologic damage.
Congenital fusion of splenic tissue with a gonad constitutes a splenic developmental anomaly. Gonadal and scrotal abnormalities have no axis.
Inherited multinodular enlargement of the thyroid gland.
Renal epithelial malignancy defined by MiT-family gene rearrangements.
Benign female reproductive tract epithelial-stromal neoplasm, typically ovarian; reproductive organs have no axis.
Inherited magnesium transport disorder, predominantly involving renal tubular reabsorption. Intestinal dysfunction and other organ damage vary by subtype.
CNS germ cell malignancy; suprasellar or bifocal involvement directly causes diabetes insipidus or pituitary hormone loss in approximately 30-50%, depending on site distribution.
Congenital platelet and megakaryocyte deficiency progressing to marrow failure; scoliosis and vertebral abnormalities are annotated at 30-79%. Nevi do not imply skin dysfunction.
Skin/nail fragility and airway/conjunctival granulation define LOC syndrome; enamel hypoplasia occurred in 6/6 patients and oral mucosal blistering in 30-79%.
Defined by reduced lung volume and impaired ventilation; extrapulmonary causes vary and do not establish another axis across the group.
Disorder of ocular accommodation caused by sustained accommodative contraction.
Intellectual disability, callosal agenesis and cerebellar abnormalities define the syndrome; strabismus affects 30-79%. Cosmetic hair and facial features do not establish damage.
Congenital atrial septal defect with left-to-right shunting; dyspnea does not establish pulmonary damage, and pulmonary hypertension is occasional.
Recurrent menstruation-associated pneumothorax directly affects the pleura and lung; menstrual timing does not establish endocrine disease.
